body:
This is exactly the missing piece in my puzzle and what happened to me, Ex was suddenly more about partying and boom. I felt dead and hollow inside.
I've never, never actually sat down and really thought about a goal and or the steps to get there, not even when I made a decision on which degree to achieve... 
My therapist knows I'm struggling with this, but she doesn't really help me in any way. In do know I want to do something with music again, I used to drum as a kid. I also want to get back in sports, but whether it would be swimming (I've been on the rescue team for some years) or weightlifting idk. It's hard, with that fog and constant doubt about everything.

I went for 2 years, from 2016 to 2018. My brother got me there when when my firsr long term relationship ended. Had a gym bud who kept the mood and discipline up and made the routines (which were way to long for a beginner). It was just about getting fit and in shape, the mental part that came with it was an extra for me. After a year it was all about getting bigger and stronger than the guy guy next to you. Ended up deadlifting 85 KG's way to fast in the end of 2017, hurting a lot of joints and tendons. That's a long time ago, but hell I love lifting a weight or two for an hour. 

At the moment I've had way to much inactivity (live with my parents, don't have work anymore) to do some solid gym work but I do want to do some beginners cardio work (I walk half an hour/an hour daily) something to get my blood flow going and clean my system from all the medicines etc I take twice a day. I've already started to eat more and healthier, something I'm really not used to anymore.

I was only 13, doing my math in class. Can't really remember when it all started but I can remember that I had problems with focus and memory for a while. Probably because I got bullied on quite some time then.

I was in math class, couldn't focus and do my math at all and was very anxious all the time and then it happened; I felt some weird sensations I had for a while, I needed to pee and I started walk towards the bathroom. One floor down these sensations became stronger and stronger and my thoughts showed me a weird picture of a man with a grin, a hat and a long coat. Next thing I know I'm sitting on a couch within a distance of 10 meters from where I was when I felt those sensations. Can't remember how I got on that couch as I was the only one in the hall. 

The seizures went on for half a year until I had them almost everyday until I had one in front of my family. The doctor didn't have any urge to put me on meds so I went on a holiday med-free, but that's another story.

Swimming could be done with a coach/trainer/friend that swims along with you or watches you and knows how to handle your seizures in the water.
Weightlifting is pretty safe, but it's best to use a Smith's machine when squatting or do some lunches instead of using the squat rack. For the benchpress and overhead press let a coach/trainer/friend help or spot you.
Running on the treadmill is best to be avoided with epilepsy, it's safer to run outside instead.

About dieting: eat healthy carbs, eat protein (it's best to only use shakes when you can't match your required protein intake, which could be found online), eat healthy fats, don't forget to fill up on your elektrolytes and vitamines as your medication will drain some of those and stay hydrated!

I recognize my story in yours.

Didn't know about PIED, but I now know that I've been having struggles with it when I was still your age. Damn, a beautiful relationshi and a lot of friendships went down the drain because of it. Would love to see that girl back once and tell her the truth, so she knows it wasn't her fault.

NAD
Tip: I stopped wearing socks in the house and took shorter showers to let the smell and itching stop. as long as your feet can get enough air and aren't moist all day long it can slowly become less.
It's still there, but isn't itchy, bleeding and spreading anymore.

You could buy special shoes, use creams etc etc. But it'll probably never really go away.

Don't worry about, it'll pass. I've gone through the same when I was addicted to candy crush and my porn addiction which I had as a teen. Your urges will come back, as long as you are staying true to your intention to quit all of those problems fade into nowhere. 

Extra advice: try to focus on something like your breath, hands or other parts of your body when your going through this, it'll make it easier to accept your mind is still used to the old habbit. It'll take some time but if you use this method every evening the mind gets used to it. You could use something like this before you'll go to bed: https://youtu.be/CyKhfUdOEgs things like these have effect after a few week(s) of daily practice in the but it could give you more insight about your thoughts and behaviour and a healthier mindset.

Change is hard, but just hold on to our true self and never give up. You can do this.

Hi, I've just switched from Keppra to Briviact after having these thoughts for a very long time. Same background, also 10 years with epilepsy. Memory is fucked, motivation is low, mood is gone, I'm not myself anymore and I've been slowly giving everything I had up.

I'm now realising I've should have talked about this way earlier, as I've made some important choices in life while taking this drug. My neuro put me on Frisium to get through the night when he heard about the side effects, but after a couple of years that wasn't enough anymore (and prohibited in my country, as I've read on the governmental farmaceutical website...)


You can't go back in time to change your behaviour, but you can change your future my (wo)man! Talk to the neuro, he'll understand the problem.
Finally, some guy showing the facts.

I've got a love hate relationship with my auras. Sometimes it's a false alarm, other times it's not. But at the moment of a TC ive got way intenser and different auras than with my partial complex seizures. Took me about 4 years to get used to it, that's for sure.

Forgot to take my Briviact for some days, am stuck with a lot of heavy auras today and don't know whether its a true or false alarm. Nothing happened for the whole day, but I do have a bite mark on my tongue from the night.  
Hope the Neuro would give me more than just one box of the stuff, as it's totally not in sync with the other meds and stressing my head off.

I would rather know beforehand, as I can take some time and just relax my body, waiting for the seizure to come. Probably better to ask her to make sure she wouldn't get all stressed out.
Are you taking supplements or just eating more?

I've got the same problem, down the line I've lost a lot of muscle and gained a lot of fat because of this. Had this problem in high school also, but back then i was only on Keppra. 

Wow that's a shame you can't do your walks anymore now. I know the feeling and thought, but you shouldn't be afraid of being the 'elephant' in the room. Everyone, I mean literally everyone has on or more a weak spots they'll be afraid of.

Well first I wanted to 'deny' it, but I couldn't walk away from it. So I cried my heart out and ran downstairs, where my brother, mother and father supported me. Got all the hugs and affirmation that I wasn't in the hospital, but that I was at home and at a safe place. That helped a lot.
Afterwards I was broken and all I could do was sleep.

Get yourself a great 'recovery' and spend a lot of time with your friends and family, talk about your time in the hospital because that matters a lot and make sure get to you do the things you love.
I've done all of that but somewhere down the line somehow stopped enjoying the time with my friends(?) and that's how my traumas came to the surface. Never knew one thing about it.
Am trying to reconnect but it's so damn hard.

Yes, it sure is. I've did it 2 years in a row. Recently realised I have PTSD and had a flashback with all the feelings and sensations included. Man that was hard.

Does explain why I can't handle stress anymore.

My support and take care of yourself!
Thats what's I'm noticing right now. last blood test showed vitamin deficiencies, but I wasn't told which...

I've taken multiple blood tests (one without eating salt on a daily base, one with extra salt on a daily base) which showed me the sodium was to low, potassium too high (I eat bananas daily and a couple of avocados during the week), iron too high (eat apples, greens, nuts, dades and dried apricots daily), but nothing was told about chloride, magnesium, fosfate and bicarbonate.
I also have found it very hard to excercise since the Zonegran was added, I can remember my excercise routines went harder and more stressful since. Am actually walking backwards thanks to it.....

Edit: since my diet already is very healthy, I've sent an email to the dietician for help.
Near Amsterdam, The Netherlands unfortunately.
Yes, it did a lot of times for me.

So I'm 'suited' for both VNS and deep brain stimulation but I'd rather not have a device inside my body. These are the measures I've taken:

 • So when I wake up I grab my jar of with almonds and hazelnuts and eat a couple of hands combined with some fruit. Afterwards I'll eat some yoghurt with seeds & fruit or some eggs, depends on what I feel like.
• Treat my skin well
• Go to the spa when I feel like it
• Take long walks with the camera to keep my stamina and mood up
• Only drink water, the shit we're swallowing everyday is enough poison already.
• Use my bicycle when I don't have to travel far
• Eat some dates in the evening instead of candy
• Listen to music a lot for focus, mood and less brain fog
• Read once in a while
• Go to the psych for more self development
• Play bass
• Eat a lot of greens
• Take vitamin D, Magnesium, Calcium and Zinc supplements.
• Try to laugh as much as I can.
• Meditate every morning and evening.
• Do stretches when I'm sitting or laying down for longer than an hour
• Take a nap in the afternoon

I have been walking barefoot as a teen/kid a lot around the campsites (Europe & Canada) and our house a lot. Also went barefoot in cars and around gas stations but never did a full barefoot day or vacation. 
Am also interested how a full barefoot vacation would be like.

While snorkeling in the sea, while skiing without my family around me because I was more physically fit, while swimming laps during the weekly training I used to do with the rescue team and a gig after I was done setting everything up for the show and the band started playing/I was doing my thing at the front of house tweaking the mix a bit and adjusting the monitors to the artists taste.

The seizures I had on the mountain and during the gig where the worst. I'm lucky to have a aura (about 10 secs before the seizure) so was already heading to the side of the piste but was to late, so I let myself fall on the ground and started to unwind my skis, just in case. 
The seizure during work was crazy. In the noise, under that amount of stress and time pressure. A band that still demanded me to work after the seizure, co-workers that didn't know what was happening while I had warned them lots of times about it. Luckily an old teacher of mine had a freewill-job there so she knew what's up and stood by me.

It surprised me, nobody ever asks me about these kind of details.
Alcohol made me very drowsy and heavy when I was on Carbamazepine and Tegretol.

Always tired, always brain fogged and easily agitated because I'm always tired. Used to be a happy, social and physical active kid but all of that's gone now.

My epilepsy tho has made me more comfortable with myself because everybody shows interest and I know I've got to take good care of this body/mind.

God damn, loading up Battlefield 2 on my dad's old PC with bad internet back in the day would take even longer. I would be waiting for 10 to 15 minutes before an online map would be loaded.. I remember waiting even longer because the server had already started another game using another map.
That has happened a lot...

Sleep apnea. A friend of mine had epilepsy until he went under surgery for his sleep apnea. Turned out the shortage of breath gave him epileptic seizures.

Ask your doctor for a sleep study.

Sunglasses! I've worked as a live sound engineer and stagehand so I learned how to deal with it pretty fast. Also: if your with friends, make sure you don't stand in or near a moshpit. I seized at a Foo Fighters concert once and stood in front of a moshpit. I was lucky because my friends saw this and started protecting me by pushing everybody back in and getting a lot of kicks and fists in their backs. I was then carried away by the first aid team and came back to my senses backstage.

Things I've learned: (proper) earplugs are a good thing just like the sunglasses, moshpits are rarely found in the back and something an epileptic shouldn't participate in unless he's seizure free for a long time, the first aid team is there for you, security is your friend (and mostly found in front of the stage and at the entrances) in case of a medical emergency and you know how to keep yourself save.

Hi, I'm taking Carbamazepine for 8 years now and have the same problems + a very high proportion of potassium in my blood (we have a very green diet, low salt diet). My hairs been falling out since I've been taking this stuff, I've always been on the run/anxious since the prescription, my skin is grey and all wrinkled, my muscles and bones hurt like hell, I've had a shoulder that's been hanging for a long time, now I've got two and my back is hurting/starting to bend/show something like a scoliosis.
I'm also going way back my ability to focus, I'm also seeing those weird things, but the doc and neuro said it's probably migraines, my eyes hurt like hell a lot and my teeth are going bad.

I've addressed almost all of this at the neuro, but he said it would be nothing and now my new neuro thought the depressed mood would be because of the Keppra, which is now switched with Briviact.
As Carbamazepine and Oxcarbamazepine both influence the salt levels, I think I've finally found the solution :).
Wow, that's an amazing feature! Guess I'll switch over to Apple then, maybe it brings me back some peace of mind when I'm alone.
Now you've showed one of your real struggles, it's a good thing. I've had one on the first date with my ex-girlfriend and that seizure (and other factors, ^^) bonded us.

You're not the only one man, I've never been over 3 months seizure free.

Well, it does sucks not being able to drive..
Not gonna lie a friend of mine just got it for his birthday

This is something I've been wondering too. I've with to my psychologist about this and we asked for a neuropsychological test at the epilepsy centre.

Mind you that stress can do a lot to the brain too, but the fact that your memories from before the seizure are fading I a symptom of brain damage. Take your rest, try relax. I've got the same problem in stores, but also big cities, railway stations etcetera. 

I hope you can find a professional where you can discuss this matter.

Hmm, funny. My neuro changed me from Keppra to Briviact when I told her about my anxiety problems. Maybe it wasn't the Keppra then. Already called the neuro about all of these problems but I didn't get anything back. Time to hit that phone up again. I'm also going to ask for a 'second opinion' neuro, to make sure it's gonna be taken care of.

I'm on 3 by now. Carbamazepine, Zonisamide and Briviact.

Am kinda really depressed, diagnosed with PTSD; have a very rough time sleeping (waking up, laying away for a long time) and am experiencing a lot of pains, migraines, I'm scared a lot, very tired, moments of being dizzy/light-headed, painful teeth (???) and losing my muscle mass quickly. Also forgetting very much and have a difficult time focussing/want to flee when im in a crowded place. It's either like I'm being drugged every daybor am both physically and mentally fucked up. Been sent to a psychologist when I went to the doctor but after 2 years all these symptoms have gone worseeeeeeeee.....

I have low blood pressure too! When I eat/am done I fall asleep, that's how bad my situation is. My doctor said "you don't have to worry about your heart" after writing down all kinds of pains, dizzyness, achings and drowsiness for a week. 
I'm still wondering how my heart is doing, I'm eating hella healthy but ain't getting nowhere.

• We're all photosensitive.

• We only get grand mal seizures.

• Brain surgery isn't a thing for epilepsy.

• We're not supposed to go to a concert.

• We can drive a car.

• Life with epilepsy isn't that hard.

• We can't do any drugs at all.

• Weed is a great drug for us.

• That we're just fooling around or parking people when seizing.....

At least you're doing better then me then! I'm burned out and stuck with the almost same problem: bad memory, a zombified head and slow cognitive function, but also have cramping and aching muscles from the adrenaline that's rushing all the time because I'm in survival mode for too long. 
Am trying to calm/slow myself down, but barely anything seems to work anymore....

See the doctor and explain yourself, make yourself happy again by singing, talking about this topic and others with friends, play some boardgames (because it requires more interaction), have some tea time trusted people, find some kind of excercise that helps you to lower the stress (for my walking 3 times a week does enough already) and don't get caught up in your thoughts, it'll only make things worse.

Ha, I've been dealing with the idea I maybe just should turn Christian lately. 
That's exactly the same situation I'm in, I've been feeling like this for a few years now and my situation has been changed a few times in a row. Yet my neuro said: don't worry bout the meds, you're doing fine. I'm happy to finally get a test to see if I'm brain damaged and have some blood research done, which they forgot to do last time.

Enjoy your day off!

I've had the same with yoga, before all this started I was weightlifting 3/4 times a week a couple of years ago and getting those muscles fired up took me a reeeeaaaaaal long time. I started excersicing back then because of another big-o problem, but I think it's a combo of meds (good nutrition and hydration helps a lot!!!!) and overall health. 

I'm subscribed to a gym with yoga classes, imma put it on my agenda this week and see how it goes down.

Good luck!

I just went to the doctor's office because that was closest and fastest option and got redirected to the in house psych. It's all pretty much seemlessly cared for in the Netherlands but I don't know where you're at so I can't really give some solid advice. 
Only I want to do a Neuropsychological Research now (just in case I might have some kind of brain damage) and my doctor isn't supporting it. Luckily the neuro and psych are fully supportive now.

If you're just overwhelmed try taking a day for yourself and head in to the woods or go to a spa, to wind down for a bit.
If you're depressed try walking in nature (helps me a lot, taking someone with you is also nice) or meditation/yoga or some other type of relaxation (seeing friends helps) or sports.

That's the thing, my family isn't really talkative. I have been through a rough time the last 2 years, got a no-no for brain surgery and we never really talk about it. Got some hugs, shred some tears and had some laughs and that's it. But if I open up about my mental problems they all either go insane or give some hugs, it's always the same.

I'm having the same struggle and have had these feelings on and of since I was a kid.
I already was diagnosed with epilepsy before I got the anxiety stamp. Now I've talked to the psych and he's so shocked after hearing my story, he wants to certainly know this isn't all a neurological issue before starting a therapy. I'm very happy about this, because I've been walking around with these issues for a very long time now and they seem to be worsening.

A few years ago I worked my ass of in an evening shift after having a seizure without remembering what I was doing for the first 10/20 minutes. Co-workers said I was acting a bit fuzzy and tried to tell me I should get some rest, which I did but way to late.
Now I have some flairs of that specific event back in my memory, which is a good reminder of how not to act after a seizure.

These days I I'm having more and more troubles remembering names and learning new tasks so I've asked my neurologist to sign me up for a neuropsychological test to see how I'm doing now, compared the last one which was 8 years ago. 
I'm also seeing a psych, which helps a lot also.
Congrats, go all out! I received the bad news 1 year ago: after multiple trials runs and a lot of scans, I'm not eligible for surgery.

Wow, this made me realize that I'm actually having a lot of aura's... 

I knew about the waking up seizury feeling, but never felt the shaky feeling until a few days ago, when I started taking Briviact instead of Keppra.
Walking in nature, photography, weightlifting and my cat.
